msg.sender, the untrusted caller address controlling ownership checks and balances.
Unchecked addition c = a + b inside safeAdd (overflow risk mitigated by require(c >= a)).
Subtraction c = a - b inside safeSub (underflow guarded by require(b <= a)).

Division c = a / b inside safeDiv (division by zero guarded by require(b > 0)).

edges.reason: Owned constructor assigns the untrusted msg.sender directly to owner.
onlyOwner modifier requires msg.sender == owner before transferOwnership executes.
acceptOwnership requires msg.sender == newOwner before transferring ownership.
onlyOwner modifier restricts transferAnyERC20Token to msg.sender == owner.
transfer debits balances[msg.sender], so the caller address flows into the balances mapping.
approve writes allowed[msg.sender][spender], keying state on the caller.
transferFrom decrements allowed[from][msg.sender], keyed on the caller allowance.
approveAndCall writes allowed[msg.sender][spender] and forwards msg.sender to the callee.
transferOwnership consumes the _newOwner parameter.
transferOwnership writes the pending newOwner state variable.
acceptOwnership resets newOwner to address(0).
acceptOwnership sets owner = newOwner, completing the ownership handover.
Owned constructor sets owner = msg.sender during deployment.
LEBRON constructor assigns the token symbol.
LEBRON constructor assigns the token name.
LEBRON constructor assigns the token decimals.
LEBRON constructor assigns _totalSupply, the minted supply.
LEBRON constructor credits the whole supply to the fixed deployer address in balances.
totalSupply performs an unguarded subtraction on _totalSupply.
balances[address(0)] is subtracted from _totalSupply; if it exceeds it the result underflows.
totalSupply reads balances[address(0)] from the balances mapping.
totalSupply returns a value derived from _totalSupply.
transfer calls safeSub to debit the sender balance.
transfer calls safeAdd to credit the recipient balance.
transfer mutates the balances mapping for sender and recipient.
safeAdd performs the integer addition c = a + b.
safeSub performs the integer subtraction c = a - b.
safeMul performs the integer multiplication c = a * b.
safeDiv performs the integer division c = a / b.
transferFrom calls safeSub on the from balance.
transferFrom calls safeAdd on the recipient balance.
transferFrom mutates the balances mapping.
transferFrom decrements the allowed allowance mapping.
approve writes the tokens value into allowed[msg.sender][spender].
allowance reads the allowed mapping.
balanceOf reads the balances mapping.
approveAndCall writes allowed[msg.sender][spender] before the external call.
approveAndCall executes an external call to an untrusted spender contract.
receiveApproval is an attacker-controlled callback that can re-enter approveAndCall.
the re-entrant callback can re-write the allowed mapping after the state update.
transferAnyERC20Token performs an external transfer call on an arbitrary tokenAddress.
the arbitrary token contract can execute code/fallbacks that re-enter the rescue function.
transferAnyERC20Token sends the rescued tokens to owner in an onlyOwner function.
tokenAddress parameter is used directly as the external call target.
balanceOf uses its tokenOwner parameter to index balances.
transfer uses the 'to' parameter as recipient.
transfer uses the tokens parameter as the transfer amount.
approve uses the spender parameter as allowance key.
approve stores the tokens parameter as the allowance value.
transferFrom uses the 'from' parameter as the debited account.
transferFrom uses the 'to' parameter as the credited account.
transferFrom uses the tokens parameter as the amount moved.
allowance uses the tokenOwner parameter as lookup key.
allowance uses the spender parameter as lookup key.
approveAndCall uses the spender parameter both as allowance key and external call target.
approveAndCall uses the tokens parameter for the allowance and the callback.
approveAndCall forwards the data parameter to receiveApproval.
transferAnyERC20Token uses the tokenAddress parameter as the ERC20 contract to call.
transferAnyERC20Token uses the tokens parameter as the rescued amount.
parameter a is an operand of the unchecked addition in safeAdd.
parameter b is an operand of the unchecked addition in safeAdd.
parameter a is an operand of the subtraction in safeSub.
parameter b is an operand of the subtraction in safeSub.
parameter a is an operand of the multiplication in safeMul.
parameter b is an operand of the multiplication in safeMul.
parameter a is the dividend of the division in safeDiv.
parameter b is the divisor of the division in safeDiv.

normalization_plan.reason: tokenOwner is only used inside balanceOf to index the balances mapping, so it is collapsed into that function core node.
the 'to' parameter exists only as the recipient argument of transfer, so it is collapsed into the transfer function node.
the tokens parameter only carries the transfer amount into transfer and has no independent state meaning.
the spender parameter is only used as the allowance key inside approve.
the tokens parameter only sets the allowance value inside approve.
the 'from' parameter only selects the debited account in transferFrom.
the 'to' parameter only selects the credited account in transferFrom.
the tokens parameter only defines the transferred amount in transferFrom.
tokenOwner is only a lookup key inside allowance.
spender is only a lookup key inside allowance.
spender is both the allowance key and the external call target inside approveAndCall.
tokens only feeds the allowance write and the external callback inside approveAndCall.
data is only forwarded to the external receiveApproval callback and has no local semantics.
_newOwner is written straight into the newOwner state variable by transferOwnership.
tokenAddress directly determines the target of the arbitrary external call, so it folds into the unsafe operation.
tokens only supplies the amount passed to the external ERC20 call.
parameter a is a direct operand of the addition evaluated inside safeAdd.
parameter b is a direct operand of the addition evaluated inside safeAdd.
parameter a is a direct operand of the subtraction evaluated inside safeSub.
parameter b is a direct operand of the subtraction evaluated inside safeSub.
parameter a is a direct operand of the multiplication evaluated inside safeMul.
parameter b is a direct operand of the multiplication evaluated inside safeMul.
parameter a is the dividend of the division evaluated inside safeDiv.
parameter b is the divisor of the division evaluated inside safeDiv and determines the zero-division guard.
